subject: declaration of variables in 'transformed parameters' block

messages.author: fb383a9a8d4978b9
messages.subject: declaration of variables in 'transformed parameters' block
parts:
Hi,
I've noticed something weird with regards to the variables declaration in the 'transformed parameters' block. 

I haven't found any topic that addresses this issue. I'm not sure it's a bug, that's why I share this in a post first. If it's not a bug, then I'd like to understand what is going on...

Here's the R code mini-example that replicates the problem (all files are attached):

N <- 10
y <- rnorm(n=N,mean=1,sd=0.5)
dat <- list(N = N, y = y)
stan.file.1 <- "file1.stan"    # Compiles and runs, no problem
stan.file.2 <- "file2.stan"    # Fails
fit <- stan(file=stan.file.2,data=dat, chains=2,iter=100)

I have two STAN scripts, one that works fine ("file1.stan") and another that produces an error  ("file2.stan").

file1.stan:

data{
int<lower=0> N;
real y[N];
}
parameters{
real A_raw[N];
real B_raw[N];
real theta_A[N];
real theta_B[N];
real<lower=0> sigma_A;
real<lower=0> sigma_B;
real<lower=0> sigma_y;
}
transformed parameters{
  real A[N];
  real B[N];
  for (i in 1:N)
  {
    A[i] <- theta_A[i] + sigma_A * A_raw[i];
    B[i] <- theta_B[i] + sigma_B * B_raw[i];
  }
}
model{
theta_A ~ normal(0,2);
theta_B ~ normal(0,3);
sigma_A ~ cauchy(0,5);
sigma_B ~ cauchy(0,5);
sigma_y ~ cauchy(0,5);
A_raw ~normal(0,1);
B_raw ~normal(0,1);
for (i in 1:N)
  y[i] ~ normal(A[i]+B[i],sigma_y);
}

file2.stan is exactly the same as file1.stan, except for the 'transformed parameters' block where I declare B after manipulating A. 

transformed parameters{
  real A[N];
  for (i in 1:N)
  {
    A[i] <- theta_A[i] + sigma_A * A_raw[i];
    
  }
  
  real B[N];
  for (i in 1:N)
  {
    B[i] <- theta_B[i] + sigma_B * B_raw[i];
  }
}

Because A does not depend on B, I don't expect this to generate any issue, but I have the following error:

Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name,  : 
  failed to parse Stan model 'file2' with error message:
EXPECTATION FAILURE LOCATION: file=input; line=27, column=3
  real B[N];
  ^-- here

DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
variable "real" does not exist.
variable "real" does not exist.
Parser expecting: "}"

Why does this generate an error? 
Thanks in advance
David

On Friday, April 25, 2014 9:40:10 PM UTC-4, David Champredon wrote:
file2.stan is exactly the same as file1.stan, except for the 'transformed parameters' block where I declare B after manipulating A.

Within any block, all the variable declarations need to take place before any of the variables are defined. I think it would be harder to write the Stan parser to permit declarations anywhere in the block.

Ben

OK, if the rule is to declare all variables at the very beginning then I'll stick to it. 

What confused me was that (I don't want to sound picky, just a comment) in the 'model' block, local variables don't have to be declared at the very beginning (e.g. can be defined in a loop)

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: declaration of variables in 'transformed parameters' block
parts:
I can't find anything in the manual either these days. We might be able to do something about the error message since reserved words like "real" can't be used as variable names anyway.

A loop is considered a local block within a block so

for(i in 1:N) {
  real theta;
  // define / use theta
}

is legal but

for(i in 1:N) {
  real theta;
  // define / use theta
  real mu;
  // define / use mu
}

is illegal.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] declaration of variables in 'transformed parameters' block
parts:
You don't need to put all locals at the top of a loop. You
can just have a standalone nested block, as in:

model {
... lots of priors ...

{
vector[N] y_hat;
y_hat <- X * beta;
y ~ normal(y_hat, sigma);
}
}

And this makes y_hat local in its block.

The best place to look for behaviors is the language reference,
or roughly the second half of the manual. There's a section
"Statement Blocks and Local Variable Declarations" that describes
how variables come to be local. What's particularly confusing is
that the model block is treated as a statement block --- that's described
in the "Program block: model" section.

I made a note to clarify that in the next version of the manual as part of
the next manual issue:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/567

- Bob
